title: Edinburgh Road apartments approved; Hadati Road townhouses debated
subtitle: Also: chiropractic clinic on Eramosa Road, Clair Road drive-through sign variances, Bill 23 concerns and parkland
overview: Council approved a mixed-use development at 265 Edinburgh Road North: two seven-storey buildings with 139 apartments and a small commercial space, on a former parking lot. Council supported it {{vote:m3}}. Councillors raised questions about energy performance, shade trees, links to nearby trails and how soon construction would start. One delegate raised concerns about development charges and parkland following the province's Bill 23.

Council also approved, on the consent agenda, changes at 639 Eramosa Road to allow a chiropractic clinic {{vote:m1}}. It approved sign by-law variances for electronic drive-through menu boards at 158 Clair Road East {{vote:m2}}.

At the statutory public meeting for 140 Hadati Road, council received the report on a proposal for 24 stacked townhouse units {{vote:m4}}. This was not a decision on the application. Many residents spoke about parking, traffic, school safety, shadowing and the loss of the corner convenience store, and several councillors said they could not support the current density. Staff will report back with a recommendation at a later meeting.
Outside the motions, the mayor thanked a departing downtown business association leader, and a councillor apologized for earlier comments about consultation on a heritage matter.

decisions.detail: Council approved the Official Plan and zoning changes for two seven-storey mixed-use apartment buildings with 139 units and 188 square metres of commercial space.
Council approved the Official Plan and zoning amendments to allow redevelopment of the property as a chiropractic medical clinic.
Council approved three variances allowing electronic drive-through menu board signs visible to, and close to, residentially zoned property.
Council received the staff report on the proposed Official Plan and zoning amendments for 24 stacked townhouse units, with no decision on the application yet.

debate: On Edinburgh Road, a councillor questioned why the site did not have more units given its location next to a high school. The applicant's representative said height and density had to be balanced.

A delegate said Bill 23 could shift servicing costs to current residents and reduce parkland, and urged council to require land rather than cash for parkland at the site. Staff said the Bill 23 impacts were still being worked out and the site was small for parkland.

At Hadati Road, residents said the proposal would add street parking, traffic and shadowing near a school and a busy crossing. They also said winter snow clearing is already difficult and that the owner had not consulted neighbours. Several asked for fewer units or a smaller design.

The applicant's team said the building was placed to give separation from neighbours, that tree retention would be explored, and that the plan used the site's existing driveways. It said a mixed-use building would have been taller, and it offered to meet with neighbours.

Several councillors said they could not support the proposed density. They pointed to the limited visitor parking and the loss of a local commercial amenity, and one asked staff to check property standards at the vacant site. Staff confirmed the proposal does not conform to the Official Plan.
